review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the related simp lemmas in Spacetime/Euclidean.lean, Spacetime/TimeTranslation.lean and Covariance/Momentum.lean. The file has almost no simp attributes of its own, so the findings concern missing canonical simp lemmas and rewrites that are proved locally instead. I did not run Lean. The claims about simp behaviour are inferred from the existing simp sets, not observed. I did not recommend simp annotations for the identities that look simple but are not used as rewrite rules.

findings.problem: The simp set in Euclidean.lean already contains `@[simp] inv_R`, `@[simp] inv_t`, `one_comp` and `comp_inv`. Together these push `(1 : E)⁻¹` or `euclideanPullback` of the identity to `LinearIsometry.inv (1 : O4)`. Nothing in the simp set simplifies that term. The missing normalization lemma is declared here as a plain, misnamed (outside the `LinearIsometry` namespace) lemma. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, so the use at line 220 has to cite it by hand in `simp only [QFT.inv_R, QFT.inv_t, LinearIsometry_inv_one, LinearIsometry.one_apply]`. Plain `simp` therefore leaves the term `LinearIsometry.inv 1` stuck wherever it appears in other files.
findings.proposed_change: Move the lemma into `namespace LinearIsometry` in Spacetime/Euclidean.lean, next to `one_comp` and `comp_inv`. Name it `inv_one` and mark it `@[simp]`. Its proof is the existing one: `comp_inv 1` plus `one_comp`. The orientation is a safe normal form, because it rewrites a compound term to the atom `1`. No other simp lemma has the left-hand side `LinearIsometry.inv 1`, so there is no competing rule. After the move, the `h_transl_eq` proof can use `simp` or the shorter `simp only [QFT.inv_R, QFT.inv_t, LinearIsometry.inv_one, LinearIsometry.one_apply]`.
findings.benefit: Simp-based proofs about the inverse of the identity Euclidean motion normalize automatically. This removes a hand-cited lemma and a stuck `LinearIsometry.inv 1` term. The lemma is also found in the namespace where users look for it.

findings.excerpt:
lemma freeCovariance_eq_kernel (m : ℝ) (x y : SpaceTime) :
    freeCovariance m x y = freeCovarianceKernel m (x - y) := by
findings.problem: The rewrite `freeCovariance m x y = freeCovarianceKernel m (x - y)` is used as the canonical form for every kernel integral. It is not a simp lemma and is not available early. Its proof is re-done as an anonymous local `have h_transl_inv` at line 392, inside `schwartz_cross_covariance_decay_real`, which comes before the lemma in the file. A third copy appears in Covariance/Momentum.lean (line 1870). Each copy unfolds three definitions and then runs `simp only [zero_sub, norm_neg]`. The lemma is applied only by an explicit `rw` (line 573) or `simp_rw [..., h_transl_inv, ...]` (line 397). Callers therefore do not share one rewrite rule, and the unfolding approach exposes the Bessel expression instead of the kernel.
findings.proposed_change: Put `freeCovariance_eq_kernel` where `freeCovarianceKernel` is defined, in Covariance/Momentum.lean before line 1623. Make it public API there. Replace the three local copies with it, for example `simp_rw [SchwartzMap.translate_apply, freeCovariance_eq_kernel, toComplex_apply]` at line 397. If the project wants a uniform normal form for kernel integrals, mark it `@[simp]`. It is safe because the right-hand side is a folded definition application, so it does not loop. It would only fire on `freeCovariance`, and the only competing unfold rules require an explicit `unfold` or `simp only [freeCovariance, ...]`.
findings.benefit: One canonical rewrite replaces three copies of the same unfolding proof. Proofs about kernel integrals stay in terms of `freeCovarianceKernel` and no longer expose `freeCovarianceBessel`. Later files no longer need to re-derive the identity.

findings.excerpt:
lemma timeShift_eq_add (s : ℝ) (y : SpaceTime) :
    TimeTranslation.timeShift s y = y + TimeTranslation.timeShiftConst s := by
  exact TimeTranslation.timeShift_eq_add_const s y
findings.problem: The time-translation rewrite rules are a hand-assembled chain with no simp interface. `timeShift_eq_add` is only a restatement of the existing `TimeTranslation.timeShift_eq_add_const`, so there are two names for one rule. `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_at_point` is `rfl` and is not tagged `@[simp]`, although a `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_apply` lemma already exists in the TimeTranslation module. The norm identity `‖timeShiftConst s‖ = |s|` and the `(-s)` form `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_neg_eq_sub` are lemmas that are not tagged `@[simp]`. Every use is an explicit `rw` chain, for example `rw [timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_at_point, timeShift_eq_add]` at line 539 and `rwa [timeShiftConst_norm, abs_of_nonneg ht]` at line 645. The `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_neg_eq_sub` proof also drops to a coordinatewise `ext i; split_ifs; ring`, because `timeShiftConst (-s) = -timeShiftConst s` is not available as a rewrite rule.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the duplicate wrapper `timeShift_eq_add` and cite `TimeTranslation.timeShift_eq_add_const` directly. In TimeTranslation.lean, state `timeShiftConst_neg : timeShiftConst (-s) = -timeShiftConst s` and `timeShiftConst_norm`. Mark them `@[simp]`, as they are directional and terminating. Also mark `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ_neg_eq_sub` `@[simp]` there, so that `timeTranslationSchwartzℂ (-s) g y` normalizes to `g (y - timeShiftConst s)` without a manual `rw` chain. Do not add `timeShift_eq_add_const` itself to the simp set unless it is checked against the existing `timeTranslationSchwartz_apply` rules, which might conflict with it.
findings.benefit: The time-translation argument of the proof reduces to `simp` plus the decay bound, instead of a stack of anonymous rewrite lemmas. One name is kept per identity, and the sign-flip and norm computations are reusable by later OS4 files.
